doc.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Singing and hoping for a film to revive early jazz
summary: He sings sparingly, enjoyed The Aviator, and hopes for another Sting-like film to spark interest.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: And when did you start — have you always been a singer?

No. And you know I try my hand at singing you know. And there’s better singers out there but to me I never want to get the audience too overwhelmed with too much singing or if people are singing, “oh why don’t you use this person?” And this way if anybody complains about the singer it’s just me, they can just complain. And I don’t really do that much but I try to just put over a song here and there in the style of some of those so- called singing band leaders.
Well you looked darned good in “The Aviator.”

Oh thanks. Well that was a lot of fun. Films are one way of turning people around. And with all these films that I’ve been associated with in the past twenty years or so I was always looking for another Sting movie. What “The Sting” did for Scott Joplin and Ragtime was fantastic. It took this music that really was in the background and young kids were learning “The Sting” which is really “The Entertainer.” And we were always hoping for a successful film that would get kids interested in early jazz and some of this pop music, hut it hasn’t happened yet, it hasn’t happened.
